title: Why Festivals Persist
sentences: Most public celebrations have outlived the beliefs that produced them.
This is usually described as decline, which misreads what they were for.
A festival synchronises a population without requiring agreement about anything.
The shared date does the work that shared conviction once did.
That function survives perfectly well after the original meaning has gone.
Attempts to abolish such occasions on rational grounds fail with regularity.
Attempts to invent replacements by decree fail even more reliably.
What cannot be legislated is the sense that everyone is doing it at once.
Commerce understood this considerably earlier than governments did.
The holiday endures, its explanation replaced roughly every second generation.
